title: Why Is Thailand Not Prosecuting Members of the Mauerberger Network?
gist: Proceeds from Cambodian scam centers linked to Yim Leak and South African fixer Benjamin Mauerberger ('Ben Smith') have been laundered into Thai markets; the author counts more than 20 listed and unlisted Thai companies holding over 26 billion baht ($778 million) in such proceeds, and argues Thailand is good at finding the money but has not prosecuted the facilitators.

themes.theme: Scam money parked in Thai companies

insights.claim: By the author's count, proceeds from Southeast Asian scam centers sit in more than 20 listed and unlisted Thai companies, in holdings worth over 26 billion baht ($778 million).
insights.speaker: Sarinee Achavanuntakul
insights.so_what: Thai-listed equities may carry hidden illicit-ownership and enforcement risk; screen shareholder registers for network-linked holders.
insights.quote: those proceeds sit in more than 20 listed and unlisted Thai companies, in holdings worth over 26 billion baht ($778 million)
insights.locator: Thailand appears in that report twice

insights.claim: Thailand is both a victim of the regional scam economy, with domestic losses above 115 billion baht ($3.5 billion) a year per a 2025 Global Anti-Scam Alliance estimate, and a destination where scam profits come to rest.
insights.speaker: Sarinee Achavanuntakul
insights.so_what: The scam economy is a macro-relevant drain on Thai households and a reputational risk for Thai capital markets.
insights.locator: Thailand appears in that report twice

insights.claim: The Whale Hunting blog by Tom Wright and Bradley Hope began exposing, in August 2025, the financial network built by Cambodian businessman Yim Leak and South African Benjamin Mauerberger, known in Bangkok as Ben Smith.
insights.speaker: Sarinee Achavanuntakul
insights.so_what: Investigative journalism is driving the enforcement agenda; further exposures could hit named Thai firms.

insights.claim: A May 2026 bipartisan U.S. House Select Committee on China report, 'Crime, Corruption, and Power,' alleges a South African fixer operated between Cambodia's crime hubs, CCP-linked developers, and Thailand's elite economy, laundering enormous illicit proceeds into Thai markets.
insights.speaker: Sarinee Achavanuntakul
entities: U.S. House Select Committee on China
insights.so_what: U.S. congressional attention raises the odds of sanctions or secondary measures touching Thai and Cambodian entities tied to the network.

insights.claim: Thailand has become effective at locating scam-linked money but has not begun prosecuting the people who helped move and launder it.
insights.speaker: Sarinee Achavanuntakul
insights.so_what: The gap between asset tracing and prosecution suggests elite protection; any shift to prosecutions would be a governance signal for Thai markets.
insights.quote: Thailand has become rather good at finding this money, but it has not begun to prosecute the people who helped to move and launder it.
insights.locator: Thailand appears in that report twice
